findings.what: The scenario panel is open at the top of every Question 3 screen, but it is titled 'Your showroom: the motor' and describes the consultation-bay motor, which has nothing to do with the DBL2 submain or C7, so he reads each part as being about the motor; give these screens a supply-and-DBL2 scenario (Ze 0.1 Ω, 4.6 kA, 230/400 V, 20 °C, the submain, C7).
The panel ends 'Your assignment ED4-01A: pack p.3, and question 4 on p.4.', which tells him where the scenario comes from; keep the source in the case file and leave it off the page.

C7's 23.8 m length is not on this screen: it appears only on the 3(h) screen, and the carried panel shows just 0.392 Ω and 1.84 V, so the part cannot be answered from its own screen or its Book example; add 'C7 runs 23.8 m' to the assumption.

findings.where: Step 9, the ticked checklist, thermal line
findings.what: The design is ticked on the far-end figures alone ('4.44 mm² of 22 mm² armour, 0.50 mm² of a 1.5 mm² cpc'), right after the screen says to check both ends, which is exactly what the card's last trap warns against; show the larger figures too: 17.39 mm² of armour for a fault at the MDB end and 1.43 mm² of cpc at the DBL2 end.

findings.where: Step 12, Keep this card, 'The showroom so far'
findings.what: The card keeps 3(f) 'minimum armour area … 5.00 mm²', a plan-length figure this lesson replaces with 4.44 mm² over every length and 17.39 mm² at the MDB end, and it lists none of the submain's new figures (20.0 m, 1.64 V, 0.95 V); show the lesson's own armour figures, or mark 3(f) as worked on the plan length.

'Take Ca as 1.00, with no credit for the cool room' has to be read twice, because nothing on the screen says what the cool room is; say it plainly, for example 'The building is at 20 °C. Take Ca as 1.00 anyway and claim nothing for the cooler air.'

findings.where: Step 4 feedback and step 7 slip hint
findings.what: He is told four times to divide a three-phase submain's drop by √3, but never why; one sentence would close the gap: the three-phase figure is the drop between lines, and a single-phase circuit sees only the line-to-neutral part, which is that figure ÷ √3.

The phase-by-phase note gives 1.97 V but never says that this is already a single-phase drop, which adds straight on without ÷ √3. Nor does it say why the note matters here: the 20% harmonic puts current in the neutral. Say both in two short sentences.

findings.where: Steps 6 and 9, after notes (near-end heat checks)
findings.what: At 2530 A and 645 A an MCB clears far faster than the 0.1 s used, so '17.39 mm²' and 'a slim pass' are cautious figures; one sourced sentence saying that the maker's let-through energy (I²t) gives the real need at high fault currents would keep him from over-sizing on a real job.

The screen never gives the disconnection time; the 0.1 s appears only in the 3(i) after note, and the general hint says just 'S = √(I² × t) ÷ k'; let the hint say to read t from where the breaker trips instantly (0.1 s).

findings.where: Step 12, Keep this card, the rule
findings.what: 'S = √(I² × t) ÷ k' never says where t comes from; add a note line such as 't from the device's time/current curve: 0.1 s once an MCB trips instantly'.

findings.where: Step 12, Keep this card, the rule notes
findings.what: 'Other circuits may drop 5%' gives no volts, unlike the lighting line; add 11.50 V single-phase and the three-phase figures, 12 V and 20 V, so the card works as a job reference.
'Table 4E1A gives 23 A in conduit for two loaded cables' names no method, and conduit in an insulated wall (Method A) gives 19 A; name Method B.

8.22 A, 1.21 A and 4.89 A are stated bare, yet they rest on assumed power factors, and the card tags 8.22 A as a practice value; add one short line, such as 'These currents rest on assumed power factors.'

Each carried part reads like '(f) Section A 3(f): minimum armour area for the DBL2 submain's armour as its cpc', with the part letter twice and 'armour' twice; trim the case-file labels to 'DBL2 submain: least armour area'.

findings.where: Steps 7-9, carried note (kit text, shown after a missed part)
findings.what: 'Carried forward at the course's figure, so one slip never spoils the rest' talks about the course; 'Carried forward at the right figure, so one slip does not spoil the rest' says the same thing plainly.
'Like a City & Guilds Section A question, with new numbers.' talks about the exercise, not the job; 'Same method, new numbers. Give the length in metres.' is enough.
'than the 5.00 mm² from the plan length in lesson 7' points at the course; say 'than the 5.00 mm² worked on the plan length alone'.
'A fault at the MDB end sees 2530.00 A' puts two decimals on a whole number (230 × 1.1 ÷ 0.1); write 2530 A.

findings.where: Step 11, note on a right answer of 40.6 m
findings.what: 'so the printed figure is 40.5 m' is an odd phrase; say 'so the answer is 40.5 m: at 40.6 m the drop just passes 6.90 V'.

Every figure in 'The showroom so far' has the same 'practice value' tag, including worked results such as 0.392 Ω, so the tag no longer tells a value to look up from one worked out from such values; worked figures could read 'worked from practice values'.

findings.where: Step 3, drop bar label at 1.21 A
findings.what: At 1.21 A the drop bar reads 'Reaches its line: 157.2 m', a length the 140 m slider cannot reach; say 'beyond 140 m'.

findings.where: Step 1, the three choices at 360 px
findings.what: The two one-line choices are centred and the wrapped one is left-aligned, so the three look mismatched; align all three left.

refresher.md promised a simple plan of the showroom with the route, a one-line diagram whose figures fill in as he works, and breaking capacity as a part of its own; the lesson has no plan, so 17.0 m and 20.8 m arrive with no picture of where they run, and breaking capacity is told in a note.
